How Entravia Raised $2.6M in its First Year

# How Entravia Raised $2.6M in its First Year

Behind the announcement: an MVP that Kasey Devine built himself, more than 60 investor conversations, and the one change to his pitch that brought in a lead investor. 

Grant Gibson

Jul 29, 2026

Kasey Devine worked out what was broken in his industry while applying for a mortgage. He had applied for a mortgage once before, years earlier, the slow way, filling out forms and collecting statements one account at a time. The second time, the banker sent a link. The portal connected to Plaid, pulled his financial data on its own, and finished in about ten minutes. The ease of the new mortgage application process stayed with him.

Devine had spent more than a decade selling for PEO companies, and none of them offered anything close to the new mortgage application process. A PEO, short for professional employer organization, is the outsourced HR provider a small business hires. “Mortgage is more heavily regulated than PEO,” he said. “Why wouldn’t this exist?” He looked for whoever had built it for PEO and found no one. That gap became the company.

### Spine is turning employee benefits into a free, AI-run back office for the small businesses that expensive PEOs and in-house HR teams have priced out.

Jason Corsello

Sep 29, 2026

Acadian Ventures is excited to announce our investment in Spine’s $3.0M seed round, alongside a syndicate that includes Y Combinator, Recursive Ventures, Meridian VC, Pioneer Fund, and other seed investors. Spine gives small and mid-size employers free, AI-run payroll, benefits administration, and compliance software — and it’s one of the more interesting business-model inversions, pushing costs away from customers and back to the brokers.

The Problem

Every small business runs into the same choice: pay for an expensive PEO, or hire an in-house HR team to manage payroll, benefits enrollment, and an ever-growing pile of compliance requirements — state registrations, ACA, ERISA, COBRA. AI-native payroll and benefits platform launches its neolab to advance the building of AI agents in the world's least forgiving domains.

NEW YORK, June 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Niural, the AI-native platform for global payroll and benefits, today announced the launch of Niural AI Labs, a dedicated research lab focused on building long-horizon agents for high-stakes domains.

"Niural AI Labs is our bet on the hardest problem in AI: agents you can trust with work where the margin for error is zero," said Nami Baral, co-founder and CEO of Niural. "Most AI is built for tasks where being wrong is cheap. We built the opposite. Payroll and benefits gave us a production environment where every decision has a right answer, a deadline, and consequences. The Lab exists to take what we have proven there and extend it into other domains companies cannot afford to get wrong."

Niural, a New York based AI native platform for global payroll, benefits, payments, and compliance, has secured an additional $21 million in strategic capital. The new money brings its total Series A funding to $52 million.

The round drew participation from FOG Ventures and NewView Capital, alongside continued investment from existing backers.

Niural plans to put the funding toward launching and developing Niural AI Labs, a research arm focused on building long-horizon AI agents for high-stakes, regulated business areas that reach beyond payroll and benefits, such as workflow orchestration and automated compliance.
